title: Zero-to-peak throughput: weight-ferry streaming and KV tricklewarmer
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Dedicated customers occasionally observe long tail cold-starts when a tenant's first traffic after a quiet period causes full model weights to be loaded and KV cache to be cold; this inflates p95/p99 latency and violates throughput-backed SLAs.

Goal: Implement a two-part, non-blocking startup strategy that (1) streams a prioritized subset of model parameters to reach usable token throughput quickly (weight-ferry streaming), and (2) gradually prefetches high-value KV entries in the background using a low-priority, tenant-aware trickle (KV tricklewarmer). The solution should reduce tail latency for first requests and reduce SLA exposure without requiring full weight residency before serving.

Scope: Dedicated fleets (reserved GPU pools) only. Initial rollout limited to Llama-family and causal transformer variants where parameter sharding and streaming is supported by the runtime. Does NOT include full snapshot migration tooling or private deployment packaging (follow-up tickets).
acceptance_criteria: Cold-start p95 latency for a cold tenant under synthetic arrival profile reduced by >= 50% compared to baseline
Initial throughput (tokens/sec) within first 5s of attach achieves >= 60% of steady-state throughput for common request sizes (<=512 tokens)
KV hit rate (tenant-specific) increases by >= 30% within first 60s after attachment compared to baseline without tricklewarmer
Feature gated behind tenant-level flags and runtime config; can be disabled per-fleet
No observable increase in OOM events or node-level memory churn during ramp (<= 5% delta), and fallback path safely serves requests if streaming fails
End-to-end integration tests (unit + staging perf) added to CI with synthetic cold-start scenarios
design_notes: Weight-ferry streaming: split model weights into three priority bands: core attention & embeddings (band A), intermediate MLP + critical kernels (band B), bulk residual and optimizer-state-like segments (band C). Serve from A+B within the first seconds via a prioritized chunked stream; background fetch for C continues to finish full residency.

Non-blocking admission: node runtime accepts tokens as soon as band A is resident; KV and band B availability increase capability gracefully. Use a capability matrix to map served features to present bands (e.g., short-seq low-reqs -> A-only path, long-seq or sampling -> prefer A+B).

KV tricklewarmer: tenant-aware ranked prefetch queue seeded by: last-requested keys (if available), model-specific hot-key profiles, and synthetic hotset sampled from production traces. The tricklewarmer operates at a low CPU priority with admission backpressure to avoid interfering with live inference.

Throughput commitments: expose a transient throughput metric during warmup composed of weight-residency fraction and KV-hit projection; autoscaler uses this to decide fast-path capacity decisions (e.g., spawn minimal hot-replicas while streaming completes).

Safety: implement a streaming integrity check + checksum for chunked weights; if corruption detected, abort streaming and fall back to full snapshot load. Streaming protocol includes per-chunk version/sequence metadata to enable resumable downloads.

Cost controls: enable rate-limited background bandwidth for weight streaming and KV prefetch to bound egress and cross-AZ cost on Dedicated networks. Defaults should be conservative and configurable per-customer commit tier.
implementation_plan: Runtime: add chunked weight loader with band prioritization and chunk sequence validation (ENG runtime team)
Scheduler: extend fleet admission controller to expose weight-residency fraction and warm-throughput projection (Autoscaling team)
KV service: implement tenant-ranked trickle prefetcher with priority queue and backpressure (KV team)
API/console: add fleet-level flags and per-tenant 'fast start' toggle; surface warmup progress in Console (Console/UI)
Integration: define wire format and protocol for streaming chunks; add unit tests and fuzzing for chunk handling
Staging: deploy to a canary dedicated fleet and run synthetic cold-start load generator (perf infra)
Rollout: start with internal beta customers, then opt-in alpha tenants, then general availability behind flags
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (dev): local runtime + unit tests, feature flag false by default
Phase 1 (internal canary): enable for infra-only tenants in a single region; monitor p50/p95/p99 and memory metrics
Phase 2 (alpha): open opt-in to <= 5 external tenants with different traffic shapes; tune trickle rate limits
Phase 3 (gradual opt-in): automatic enable for tenants with throughput-backed commitments after a green alpha
Phase 4 (GA): enable by default for new dedicated fleets, with per-customer opt-out
telemetry: alerts: cold_start_p99_exceeds_threshold; weight_stream_chunk_failure_rate > 1% over 5m; kv_trickle_backpressure_rate high
test_plan: Unit tests for chunked loader and checksum handling
Integration tests for admission gating and capability matrix transitions
Stress perf test: synthetic cold-start bursts for 100 tenants in staging; measure tail latencies and memory churn
Chaos test: abort weight stream mid-way and validate fallback correctness
Cost regression test: simulate background streaming bandwidth at different caps and measure cross-AZ egress
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: streaming bandwidth could interfere with inference traffic -> Mitigation: strict QoS and rate limiting on background streams

Risk: partial residency causes subtle model degradation in some ops -> Mitigation: capability matrix ensures unsafe ops block until required bands are present; add automatic rollback if error rate increases
Risk: KV prefetch churn evicts useful entries -> Mitigation: tenant-aware heuristics, time-decayed scoring, and admission backpressure when eviction rate rises
Risk: cost increase for heavy prefetch -> Mitigation: expose configurable prefetch budget per-tenant and tenant-tier defaults
notes: Prototype experiments (Jan 2025) showed 3x improvement in p95 for short sequence traffic when a 2-band streamer was used compared to naive full-load approach
Coordinate with SRE on deployment knobs for streaming QoS across AZs
Keep rollout conservative for tenants with strict egress budgets; provide a dashboarded estimator of expected prefetch egress
